topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the speaker's background, and presents the core learning objectives regarding cancer causation and environmental carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, mutation sources, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease, discussing the balance between intrinsic 'bad luck' mutations and environmental exposures through global epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental carcinogenesis, tumor promotion, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological, physical, and chemical agents induce neoplastic transformation through direct mutagenesis, metabolic activation, adduct formation, chronic inflammation, tumor promotion, and stage-specific tissue susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and evaluating exposure risks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the sequencing, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental approaches used to detect mutational signatures and test carcinogenicity, alongside the societal appraisal of risks versus benefits.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and final summary of the lecture's key themes before concluding the session.
